reasonable_RAO_range_definition: All finite linear six-DOF vessel response operators whose zero-lever-arm CoG translational projection h(f,theta) lies below the declared continuum envelope ||h||_2 <= G min(1,(f_c/f)^p), with G in [0,4], f_c in [0.03,1.2] Hz, p>=2, arbitrary complex phase, arbitrary frequency/heading variation below that envelope, and arbitrary cross-axis coupling. Rotational response remains arbitrary subject to the separately declared P1 Normal-Live body-rate/attitude source bounds. This is a broad deployment envelope, not one nominal hull and not a finite RAO catalog.

response_contract.zero_lever_arm_translation_projection: h is the CoG translational projection of the parent six-DOF RAO. On the theorem's zero-lever-arm branch, rotational motion does not create a fictitious translational lever-arm acceleration.
response_contract.shipping_sigma_band_source_note: The lower endpoint is the exact binary32 value of the deployed 0.01f source literal; the physical label remains 0.01 Hz.
response_contract.uniform_moment_theorem: For every member of the continuum parameter box and every admissible directional spectrum, tr(M_disp)<=G^2 H_s^2/16, tr(M_vel)<=(2*pi*f_c)^2 G^2 H_s^2/16, and tr(M_acc)<=(2*pi*f_c)^4 G^2 H_s^2/16. Because these bounds are monotone in G and f_c and p>=2, the single envelope corner (G_max,f_c_max,p_min) proves the whole RAO range; it is not a representative RAO.

engineering_basis.high_frequency_rolloff_reason: Linear monohull RAO models attenuate sufficiently short waves; the theorem assumes the deliberately weak second-order-or-faster magnitude rolloff needed to make acceleration response moments finite.
engineering_basis.gain_upper_rationale: G<=4 is a 12.04 dB bound on the norm of the full three-axis CoG translational response vector, allowing substantial resonance while remaining a finite robust deployment envelope.
engineering_basis.rolloff_corner_rationale: The upper corner is the deployed 1.2 Hz wave-tuning safety ceiling; source comments identify 0.83 s as shorter than a sea a hull is intended to respond to. Lower response corners are included automatically.
engineering_basis.external_reference: Jensen, Mansour & Olsen, Ocean Engineering 31 (2004) 61-85, doi:10.1016/S0029-8018(03)00108-2, gives closed-form monohull heave/pitch/roll response functions from principal dimensions and operational profile; it motivates using a response family rather than one identified hull but is not treated as a proof that every vessel satisfies this deployment envelope.
